our_title: Thread creation failure with launched slaves still hangs; master never joins start-up barrier
ran: repro/COR-09 (spawn 4, LD_PRELOAD shim failing the N-th pthread_create), pristine 7.0.18 ASan: FAIL_AT=1 -> 'threadContextInit: cannot create thread (1)', 'spawn (4) returned 1', 'exit done', rc=0, no leak (fixed); FAIL_AT=2 and 3 -> error printed then hang (timeout 15 s, rc=124). gdb on FAIL_AT=2: slave 'threadWaitBarrier1 common_thread.c:331' in pthread_cond_wait, master '__pthread_cond_destroy ... threadContextExit3 common_thread.c:193 <- threadContextInit :146'. ThreadSanitizer tree (pristine 7.0.18, -O1 -fsanitize=thread, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/work18/G06-threads-context/tsan), FAIL_AT=3: 6 reports: data race write common_thread.c:145 (contptr->thrdnbr = thrdnum, no lock) vs read :322 under lock in threadWaitBarrier1; pthread_mutex_destroy/pthread_cond_destroy (:193-194) while T1 waits in pthread_cond_wait (:331); 'destroy of a locked mutex'; and 'free ... contextThreadInit2 common_context.c:202' racing with T1's read at :338 (use after free of the ThreadContext). Patched (0002): FAIL_AT=1,2,3 -> 'spawn (4) returned 1', 'exit done', rc=0 on 32/64-bit ASan trees, spawn 8 with FAIL_AT=2,5,8 rc=0; TSan patched tree (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/work18/G06-threads-context/tsanp): 0 reports for FAIL_AT=0,1,2,3, check_common_thread and check_scotch_context at 4 threads 0 reports. check_common_thread, check_common_random, check_scotch_context, check_scotch_graph_map at 1/2/4 threads x SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=0/1 on the 32- and 64-bit trees: 48/48 rc=0 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/work18/G06-threads-context/check.log); both trees 0 warnings.
severity_note: Same as the review: reachable from every library call (contextCommit creates the thread pool) when thread creation fails (EAGAIN under ulimit/cgroup pressure); a hang is worse than the failed call it replaces, but the trigger is a resource exhaustion.
evidence: common_thread.c:145-148 'contptr->thrdnbr = thrdnum; /* Terminate all threads that have been launched to date */ threadContextExit3 (contptr); memFree (desctab); return  (1);' -- thrdnbr = thrdnum counts the master, which never enters the start-up barrier on this path, so the thrdnum - 1 slaves in threadWaitBarrier1 (:322 'if (barrnbr == contptr->thrdnbr)', :333 same test after wake-up) never reach the count; Exit3 :186-190 'do { ... barrnbr = contptr->barrnbr; ... } while (barrnbr != thrdnbr);' is satisfied by the slaves' barrier arrivals (barrnbr == thrdnum - 1), not by their termination acknowledgements, then :193-194 destroy cond/mutex under waiters.
upstream_change: 86559b85 Bugfix: abort cleanly when cannot start thread system [report R. Perry]

upstream_fix_review.details: Right: desctab is now freed (:147) and the lock features are destroyed even when no slave was launched (Exit3 :193-194), which fixes the leak for FAIL_AT=1; threadWaitBarrier1 reads thrdnbr under the lock, which a reduced count needs. Wrong: the reduced count (:145, thrdnbr = thrdnum) includes the master, but the master never takes part in the start-up barrier on the failure path, so the barrier can never complete (slave positions are 1..thrdnum-1); the in-loop 're-check' at :333 can therefore never fire. Exit3's spin (:186-190) counts barrier arrivals as terminations, exits early and destroys the cond/mutex with waiters: glibc blocks forever in pthread_cond_destroy (same hang as 7.0.17, new place); with other libcs/TSan the slaves are left parked on destroyed primitives inside a ThreadContext that contextThreadInit2 frees (common_context.c:202): use after free (TSan report). Also :145 writes thrdnbr without the lock while slaves read it under the lock (data race; 'volatile' added to common_thread.h does not make it race-free). Even with a slave-only count (thrdnum - 1) Exit3 would stay racy: barrnbr can equal the slave count from barrier arrivals stored before the reduction, before the last slave resets it. Typo 'shutdow' copied from Exit2.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 0002 did what is still missing: lock, reduce thrdnbr, master joins threadContextBarrier, then exits (the barrier resets barrnbr to 0, so the exit spin counts only terminations). His version is better on structure (dedicated Exit3 that always destroys the lock features, so no special case for thrdnum == 1; barrier reading thrdnbr under lock). The rebased 0002 keeps all of his code and adds only the locked reduction and the master's barrier call (3 lines): best of both.

review_accuracy: accurate (mechanism, both symptoms, location); carried over.
first_pass_critique: Status, method and evidence correct; its diff (firstpass_work/COR/diffs/common_thread.c.diff) matches its sketch and is behaviourally the same as patches/0002. Gaps: it did not run ThreadSanitizer on the barrier change, did not check the other init paths (contextThreadInit2 frees thrdptr correctly; SCOTCH_contextThreadImport1 has no failure path), and did not build 64-bit. Its tradeoff note 'depends on the started threads being reachable by the barrier' is right: they can only be in threadContextBarrier() or before it, and the comparison against thrdnbr is made under the lock, so every interleaving completes.

evidence: common_thread.c:141 'corenum = threadProcessCoreNum (contptr, (coretab != NULL) ? coretab[thrdnum] : thrdnum);' ; :926 'corenbr  = threadProcessCoreNbr (contptr);' ; :927 'thrdnum %= corenbr;'

upstream_fix_review.details: Right: both call sites (:141, :153) now go through the mask lookup, and threadProcessCoreNum() uses threadProcessCoreNbr() so the non-Linux build reduces the same way. Breaks: the documented coretab value -1 ('thread not bound', s_l.tex:8224-8226) reaches threadProcessCoreNum(); '-1 % corenbr' stays -1, the loop 'for (corenum = 0; thrdnum >= 0; ...)' (:930) is not entered and corenum = 0 is returned, so the thread is bound to CPU 0 even outside the process mask (run: taskset 2-3 -> CPU 0). Any negative entry does the same. The block comment (:912-916) still speaks of a 'thread number'. The routine's first-pass sketch in our 7.0.17 critique predicted exactly this bug.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 0004 had the same call sites plus 'if (corelog < 0) return (-1);', a renamed parameter (corelog) and a rewritten block comment. The rebased 0003 adds only the guard and the comment, keeping his parameter name. Ours was better (no regression); his keeps the non-Linux reduction in one place, which ours did not.

review_accuracy: accurate; its 'Fix:' (map coretab entries through the same mask-based lookup) is what the documentation already promises and what patches/0004 does. Its secondary point (setaffinity result ignored) is true but the maintainer ignores it in threadProcessStateRestore() too; binding is best-effort (alt C provided).
first_pass_critique: Preferred option A (treat entries as physical ids, validate against the mask) contradicts the documented semantics (s_l.tex:8179-8191: logical indices, modulus reduction) and INSTALL.txt:585-591; method says 'reproduced' but both options are marked 'Not tested'. Its option B sketch 'corenum = threadProcessCoreNum (contptr, coretab[thrdnum])' would introduce a bug: for the documented -1 ('not bound'), thrdnum %= corenbr keeps -1, the for-loop body never runs and corenum ends up 0, i.e. the thread is pinned to the first core instead of left unbound. patches/0004 makes threadProcessCoreNum() return -1 for negative input.

fix_options.label: a. Reseed the context generator when the option is set (API, Parse, environment); SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC env implies the fixed seed
fix_options.summary: library_context.c: SetNum(RANDOMFIXEDSEED, 1) calls intRandSeed (randptr, 1) (the COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED seed); SetNum(DETERMINISTIC, 1) goes through SetNum(RANDOMFIXEDSEED, 1); context.c: contextOptionsInit sets rafival = 1 when deteval != 0 (as the API does) and reseeds when rafival != 0.
fix_options.tested: build_nofs_alt: 0 warnings; -Cf, SCOTCH_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED=1, SCOTCH_DETERMINISTIC=1 all reproducible across runs (3 trials); unconfigured runs still vary.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Behaviour change needing the maintainer's decision: (1) contextOptionsInit runs at every CONTEXTINIT, i.e. at every library call on a plain (non-container) object, so with the option on the shared global generator is reseeded before every call and successive calls on the same graph give identical results, whereas with the compile-time flag the stream continues across calls (SCOTCH_randomReset exists for users who want the restart); (2) reseeding the global generator from one context affects all contexts that use it.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Smallest change that makes the documented knobs do what README.md:115 and s_l.tex:7913 say; whether the run-time option should mean 'seed once per process' (which needs intRandInit to know the option, i.e. moving the random initialization from contextInit() to contextCommit() and giving intRandInit a flag) is his call. Not sent as a commit for that reason.

fix_options.label: b. Honour the option at first generator initialization only
fix_options.summary: Move intRandInit() of the global generator from contextInit() to the first contextCommit()/contextRandomClone() and pass it the option value (seed 1 if fixed, time(NULL) otherwise), so the semantics equal the compile-time flag.
fix_options.tested: untested: no diff; needs an API change of intRandInit() (common layer) and a change of the init order in context.h CONTEXTINIT and SCOTCH_contextInit; the maintainer's design choice.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Exact equivalence with COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED; but the option value is only known after contextOptionsInit, and the option set later through SCOTCH_contextOptionSetNum would have no effect on an already-initialized generator unless it reseeds (option a).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Cleaner semantics, larger change across common_integer.c / common_context.c / context.h.

notes: 7.0.17 status: still-present -> 7.0.18 status: still-present. No upstream change to intRandInit / contextOptionsInit / the option setters.
